buessen-sparse-definition: Section 'Sparse Trotterization' (p.2): k>1 linearly connected nodes, interconnect used at fraction 1/n, Eq. 2 with step n*dt between nodes. The paper defines the scheme.
buessen-models-and-setup: Models (p.2) and Results (p.3): XY model with J=1 and domain wall state, TFI with h=0.5 and h=2.0 from a uniform state, k equal sections on linear nodes, reference step 0.1. Read in context.
buessen-reference-state-benchmark: Results (p.2-3): all approximations are benchmarked against the uniform Trotter state with step 0.1, and F_ref = |<psi_ref|psi>|^2. So the fidelities measure closeness to that reference, not to the exact state. This follows from the definition.
buessen-stochastic-setup: Main text p.4: normal distribution with mean and sigma, average over 1000 randomized instances. Supplement p.7: values below the reference step are replaced by it. Fig. 5 caption (p.5): L=18, k=3, step 0.1. The anchor 'p.3-4' is approximate (main text is p.4).
buessen-limits-1d: Conclusion (text p.5; anchor p.4 approximate): the work focused on one-dimensional models, and larger models are future work with more inter-node communication expected. buessen-scope-ising-xy: Abstract (p.1) and Models (p.2): the paper simulates the XY model and the transverse-field Ising model, two one-dimensional chains.
muta-definition: Section III (p.3): the paper defines Q_{i,k}, triangles T_{i,j,k}, MuTA layer (n,i) of wires of length 5, depth d as d layers, and concatenation by identifying outputs with inputs.
muta-setup-measurement-flow: Section II (p.2): the measurement form cos(a)X + sin(a)Y is assumed, angles adapt by flow, and the paper considers only graphs with flow, leaving Pauli flow aside for simplicity.
muta-property2-universality: Section III, Property 2 (p.3): the proof uses single-qubit gates plus IsingXX(phi) with phi not in pi*Z as a universal set (cited, Refs. 35, 36), then builds both gate types on MuTA (Table I, Euler decomposition, Appendix B Eq. B1). The conditions are carried by the quotes. The universality of the gate set is cited, the rest is proved in the paper.
muta-property3-entanglement: Section III, Property 3 (p.3; anchor p.4 approximate): the proof translates the layer to a circuit (Appendix B, Eq. B2), shows no entanglement at 0 or pi, and shows a mixed reduced state (Tr rho^2 < 1) otherwise. The paper defines 'entangling' for the claim.
muta-property5-scalability: Section III, Property 5 (p.4): at most as many parameters as qubits, summed over layers to 4*sum(n_l) <= 4dn. The proof is short and the step from qubits to the factor 4 is not spelled out, but it is the paper's own counting argument. The value correctly limits the claim to a parameter count.
muta-property6-monotonic: Section III, Property 6 (p.4): the proof says 'for weak monotonicity, it is sufficient to show that the expansions do not reduce the set' and shows that for the three expansions. So the proved result is weak (non-decreasing) monotonicity only, and strict increase is not shown. The term 'admissible triangles' is not defined in the paper. The value already states the weak scope. HIGH holds only if the stored wording keeps 'weak'. Flag for the coordinator.
muta-property7-two-colorable: Section III, Property 7 (p.4): the proof shows the graph is bipartite by column parity, with 2-colorable equivalent to bipartite. The purification advantage clause is cited to Ref. 37 and is not proved here. Consider dropping that clause from the value.
muta-noisy-data-setup: Fig. 4 caption (p.6): noiseless test data, 60 and 200 training steps, 5 runs on Haar-random datasets, N=20 and N=100 split evenly between training and testing.
muta-qfi-classifier-caveat: Section IV-C (p.7): the authors say QFI for a known operator needs no machine learning, and that their example only suggests MB-QML can classify when no operational definition exists. The value keeps the hedge.
muta-hea-setup-heuristics: Section V (p.8) and Fig. 9 and 10 captions: angles {0, pi/4, pi/2} (homodyne gives 0 and pi/2, the T state adds pi/4), the epsilon-greedy and DQN heuristics, and the target gate (T x 1)IsingXX(-pi/4) on a (2,0) layer with injected T states. The clause 'discrete optimization can be NP-hard' is an uncited field remark inside the value. It does no harm but is not setup.
muta-translation-flow-paths: Appendix B (p.12-13): items 1 to 4 each carry a short proof, and the translation algorithm is built by induction over the measurement order. The conditions (flow, |I|=|O|) are in the quotes and the value.
muta-layer-circuit-form: Appendix B (p.13): Eq. B1 is derived step by step for the (2,0) layer from the translation algorithm. Eq. B2 for a general layer follows from the same algorithm and is stated with the replacement rule for unconnected rows. The derivation for B2 is brief.
muta-theorem-a2-relu: Appendix A (p.12): Theorem A.2 with Definitions A.3 and A.4 and a proof of both directions (affine inverse, then the preimage argument). 'Monotonically expressive' is the authors' own definition, which the value states.
muta-focus-deterministic: Section VI (text p.9; anchor p.10 approximate): the paper says it focused on deterministic MBQC and leaves trainable probabilistic angle adaptation as an open question.
muta-code-availability: Data availability (p.10): all simulations are in Python at github.com/mentpy/mentpy.
muta-hardware-scope-photonic-gkp: Section V (text p.8; the stored anchor p.9 is wrong): 'Here, we focus on photonic GKP computation'.

callison-mlqae-description: Section 2.5 (p.7): the paper describes MLQAE as Grover-depth d_j circuits not controlled on another register, N_shot shots per depth, the likelihood of Eq. 21 combined into Eq. 22, and numerical maximization.
callison-fisher-information: Section 2.5.1 (p.8) states Eq. 23 and Appendix A (p.24-26) derives it: single-shot score, expectation, then additivity over shots at each depth. callison-analysis-limits: Section 6 (p.23) says the analysis assumed the Bernstein-von Mises conditions and was not completely rigorous. Section 3.1 (p.13) says noise beyond depth limitation is not considered. Appendix B (p.26) says the scaling analyses consider only power-of-2 maximum depth.
callison-simulation-setup: Section 3.2 (p.13-14): no full circuit simulation, good-state counts drawn from a binomial, log-likelihood maximized on a grid of 3/epsilon regular points where the factor 3 was chosen arbitrarily. callison-depth-jittering-definition: Section 5 (p.19-20): Algorithm 2 and its text define depth jittering with a logarithmic spread coefficient, c=2 chosen arbitrarily, and the paper calls the logarithmic spread a heuristic choice.

callison-scope-depth-limited: Abstract (p.1) says the analysis covers scenarios where circuit depth is limited, and Section 3.1 (p.12-13) is that analysis.
canonici-framing-classical-ml: Section V (text p.9; anchor p.7 is wrong): the last conclusion paragraph says the work is framed as classical ML for quantum data, with QML models left to future work.

The determinism itself is the cited flow theorem (Danos and Kashefi), not proved here.
theory_low.callison-scaling-assumption: Section 2.5.1 (p.9-10): the normal approximation rests on the Bernstein-von Mises regularity conditions, which the paper says in Section 6 are not shown to hold ('not completely rigorous'). The speedup scaling follows from Suzuki et al.'s schedule, so it is conditional and partly prior work.
theory_low.callison-shots-formula-scope: Section 3 (p.10-11): Eq. 40 comes from the same asymptotic normal approximation plus an erfinv approximation, and the paper restricts to small precision to avoid contradicting that assumption. It is approximate, not proved.
theory_low.callison-depth-limited-speedup: Section 3.1 (p.12-13): the O(d) speedup is derived from Eqs. 41 to 48 and the paper itself writes 'assuming the Bernstein-von Mises theorem holds'. It is an approximate scaling argument, not a proof.
theory_low.callison-tradeoff-exponential-schedule: Section 3.1 (p.12) and Appendix B (p.26): the claim is an argument from the scaling analysis, compared to the Giurgica-Tiron et al. result (cited, Ref. 25). Appendix B shows the base tends to 2 but the scaling analyses assume a power-of-2 maximum depth. Not a proved result.
theory_low.callison-exceptional-explanation: Section 4 (p.15-19): an explanation in terms of Bernstein-von Mises conditions i and ii failing and of two close likelihood peaks. The paper only says the intuition is 'approximately confirmed' against simulation, and the exceptional region extends past the prediction. It is an interpretation checked on figures, not a proof.

value_replace.muta-property6-monotonic: The paper states Property 6 (Monotonicity of expressivity) for three expansions of a MuTA (adding layers, adding disconnected wires, adding admissible triangles together with an extra layer), and its proof shows weak monotonicity: the expansions do not reduce the set of implementable gates.
value_replace.muta-property7-two-colorable: The paper states Property 7 that the graph of any MuTA is 2-colorable, because a graph is 2-colorable if and only if it is bipartite and collecting even columns and odd columns gives a bipartition.
value_replace.muta-hea-setup-heuristics: The authors state their hardware-efficient setup: the permitted measurement angles are 0, π/4 and π/2, and they propose two heuristics for the discrete optimization over measurement patterns, a slice-wise epsilon-greedy search and a deep Q-learning agent, tested on learning the gate (T ⊗ 1) · IsingXX(−π/4) on a single (2, 0)-MuTA layer with injected T states.
